hints.title: Cumulative Salary Budgeting
hints.text: Candidates must be hired by ordering candidates within each experience tier by lowest salary first.

hints.title: Window Running Total
hints.text: Compute a running total of salary for seniors ordered by salary and employee identifier.

hints.title: Deduct Senior Expenditure
hints.text: Filter seniors whose cumulative sum is under seventy thousand, determine the remaining budget, and filter juniors similarly.

hints.title: Complete Query
hints.text:
```mysql
WITH RankedCandidates AS (
    SELECT
        employee_id,
        experience,
        salary,
        SUM(salary) OVER(PARTITION BY experience ORDER BY salary, employee_id) AS running_salary
    FROM Candidates
),
Seniors AS (
    SELECT employee_id, running_salary
    FROM RankedCandidates
    WHERE experience = 'Senior' AND running_salary <= 70000
),
Juniors AS (
    SELECT employee_id, running_salary
    FROM RankedCandidates
    WHERE experience = 'Junior'
      AND running_salary <= (70000 - COALESCE((SELECT MAX(running_salary) FROM Seniors), 0))
)
SELECT 'Senior' AS experience, COUNT(*) AS accepted_candidates FROM Seniors
UNION ALL
SELECT 'Junior' AS experience, COUNT(*) AS accepted_candidates FROM Juniors;
```

complexity.time: O(N log N) sorting candidates by salary for cumulative sum
complexity.space: O(N) for ranked candidate window partition
complexity.notes: Window running total computes exact candidate hiring tiers.
complexity.whyNaiveFails: Hiring seniors greedily without running total requires quadratic subqueries.
complexity.spaceTimeTradeoff: Window aggregation sorts rows once per partition.
complexity.interviewerExpectation: Candidate should partition by experience, compute running salary, and handle empty senior pool gracefully.

solutions.code:
import pandas as pd

def count_candidates(candidates: pd.DataFrame) -> pd.DataFrame:
    seniors = candidates[candidates['experience'] == 'Senior'].sort_values(by=['salary', 'employee_id'])
    seniors['running'] = seniors['salary'].cumsum()
    accepted_seniors = seniors[seniors['running'] <= 70000]
    spent = accepted_seniors['running'].max() if not accepted_seniors.empty else 0
    
    juniors = candidates[candidates['experience'] == 'Junior'].sort_values(by=['salary', 'employee_id'])
    juniors['running'] = juniors['salary'].cumsum()
    accepted_juniors = juniors[juniors['running'] <= (70000 - spent)]
    
    return pd.DataFrame({
        'experience': ['Senior', 'Junior'],
        'accepted_candidates': [len(accepted_seniors), len(accepted_juniors)]
    })
